units.title: Gaussian integration by parts on its integrable domain
units.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure, and let \(\gamma=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\). Fix a function \(f:E\to\mathbb R\) that is Fréchet differentiable everywhere and any direction \(v\in E\). Assume that each of \(f\), \(x\mapsto\langle x,v\rangle f(x)\), and \(x\mapsto Df(x)[v]\) is absolutely integrable under \(\gamma\). Then the weighted value and the directional derivative have the same Gaussian integral. No positive-dimension or unit-direction restriction is imposed.
assumptions: \(E\) is a real inner-product normed space of finite dimension, with its Borel measurable structure. Its completeness is derived.
\(\gamma\) is the actual centered Gaussian probability with identity covariance on \(E\).
\(f:E\to\mathbb R\) is Fréchet differentiable at every point, and \(v\in E\) is arbitrary, including zero.
\(\int_E|f|\,d\gamma<\infty\), \(\int_E|\langle x,v\rangle f(x)|\,d\gamma<\infty\), and \(\int_E|Df(x)[v]|\,d\gamma<\infty\). All three belong to this theorem’s stated domain.

steps.title: Identify and differentiate the actual Gaussian density
steps.text: Write \(d=\dim_{\mathbb R}E\). The existing Gaussian density theorem identifies \(\gamma\) with \(\omega\,dx\). Differentiating the exponential of the squared norm gives the directional derivative shown below; the normalizing constant is independent of the evaluation point.
steps.lean:
private def standardWeight (x : E) : ℝ :=
  ((Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi))⁻¹) ^ Module.finrank ℝ E * Real.exp (-‖x‖^2 / 2)

private theorem standardWeight_pos (x : E) : 0 < standardWeight x := by
  dsimp [standardWeight]
  positivity

private theorem standardGaussian_density :
    stdGaussian E = (volume : Measure E).withDensity
      (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (standardWeight x)) := by
  have h := AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.IsotropicGaussianDensity.map_sqrt_smul_stdGaussian_eq_withDensity
    (E := E) 1 (by norm_num)
  simpa only [Real.sqrt_one, one_smul, Measure.map_id', mul_one,
    standardWeight] using h
steps.detail: Literal density definition and identification. The density derivative is proved in the same module at lines 50–67 and is used in the next excerpt.

steps.title: Transfer the stated integrability domain to Lebesgue measure
steps.text: Because \(\omega\) is positive, Gaussian integrability of a scalar function gives Lebesgue integrability after multiplication by \(\omega\). Apply this to the three assumed functions. The density derivative identifies the third weighted product, with its minus sign.
steps.formula: \omega f,\quad\omega Df[ v ],\quad D\omega[v]f=-\omega\langle x,v\rangle f\quad\text{are Lebesgue integrable}.
steps.lean:
let : CompleteSpace E := FiniteDimensional.complete ℝ E
  have hDw (x : E) : fderiv ℝ (standardWeight : E → ℝ) x v =
      -standardWeight x*inner ℝ x v := by
    rw [(standardWeight_hasFDerivAt x).fderiv]
    simp only [smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, innerSL_apply_apply]
  have hwp := standardGaussian_weighted_integrable hfi
  have hwdf := standardGaussian_weighted_integrable hdf
  have hwxf := standardGaussian_weighted_integrable hxf
  have hDwf : Integrable (fun x => fderiv ℝ (standardWeight : E → ℝ) x v*f x)
      (volume : Measure E) := by
    convert hwxf.neg using 1
    ext x
    rw [hDw]
    simp only [Pi.neg_apply]
    ring

steps.title: Move the derivative and cancel the sign
steps.text: The two differentiable functions \(\omega\) and \(f\) satisfy the full-space integration-by-parts domain. Transfer the derivative from \(f\) to \(\omega\), substitute the derivative from step 1, and convert both weighted Lebesgue integrals back to Gaussian integrals.
steps.lean:
have hparts := integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable hDwf hwdf hwp
    (fun x _ => (standardWeight_hasFDerivAt x).differentiableAt)
    (fun x _ => hf x)
  rw [standardGaussian_weighted_integral, standardGaussian_weighted_integral]
  calc
    (∫ x, standardWeight x*(inner ℝ x v*f x)) =
        -(∫ x, fderiv ℝ (standardWeight : E → ℝ) x v*f x) := by
      rw [← integral_neg]
      apply integral_congr_ae
      filter_upwards with x
      rw [hDw]
      ring
    _ = ∫ x, standardWeight x*fderiv ℝ f x v := hparts.symm

units.title: Hermite products of correlated Gaussian projections
units.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure, and let \(\gamma=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\). Let \(u,v\in E\) satisfy \(\|u\|=\|v\|=1\), and put \(\rho=\langle u,v\rangle\). Let \(H_k\) denote the unnormalized probabilists’ Hermite polynomial, defined by \(H_0=1\) and \(H_{k+1}(t)=tH_k(t)-H_k^{\prime}(t)\). For every pair of natural degrees \(i,j\), the literal product \(x\mapsto H_i(\langle u,x\rangle)H_j(\langle v,x\rangle)\) is absolutely integrable under \(\gamma\). Its integral is \(i!\rho^i\) if \(i=j\), and zero if \(i\ne j\). Both degrees can be zero, and coincident or antipodal unit directions are included.
assumptions: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure; \(\gamma\) is its centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability.
\(u,v\) are actual unit vectors in the same carrier. There is no linear-independence, orthogonality or nonsingular two-dimensional density assumption.
\(i,j\in\mathbb N\) are arbitrary. The polynomials have integer coefficients evaluated in \(\mathbb R\) through the canonical coefficient map.
The correlation is the actual inner product \(\rho\in[-1,1]\). Both endpoint values and zero are allowed. Product integrability is a conclusion.
conventions: When \(i=j=0\), the natural zeroth power gives integral one, even if \(\rho=0\). At \(u=v\), the equal-degree value is \(i!\); at \(u=-v\), it is \(i!(-1)^i\).
Dimension one is allowed. In dimension zero no unit vectors exist, so the unit-vector hypotheses are vacuous; the theorem does not create such vectors.

steps.title: Obtain integrability from polynomial Gaussian moments
steps.text: Every real polynomial ridge belongs to \(L^2(\gamma)\) by the existing Gaussian polynomial theorem. The product of any two such ridges is integrable by Cauchy–Schwarz. An extra factor \(\langle u,x\rangle\) is absorbed into the first polynomial, so the same result will supply the weighted Stein integrand.
steps.formula: p(\langle u,\cdot\rangle),q(\langle v,\cdot\rangle)\in L^2(\gamma)\ \Longrightarrow\ p(\langle u,\cdot\rangle)q(\langle v,\cdot\rangle)\in L^1(\gamma).
steps.lean:
private theorem ridge_L2 (p : Polynomial ℝ) (w : E) :
    MemLp (fun x => p.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ) 2 (stdGaussian E) := by
  obtain ⟨hf, _⟩ :=
    GaussianPolynomialDifferentiation.actual_gaussian_polynomial_ridge_L2_frechet_derivative
      (E := E) p
  exact hf w

private theorem ridge_product_integrable (p q : Polynomial ℝ) (u v : E) :
    Integrable (fun x => p.eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ * q.eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ) (stdGaussian E) :=
  (ridge_L2 p u).integrable_mul (ridge_L2 q v)
steps.detail: Literal excerpt from the unchanged historical public-path candidate. The complete module supplies the named local facts and remains available for whole-module review.

steps.title: Supply the full Stein domain for the product
steps.text: For a real polynomial \(q\), set \(f(x)=H_i(\langle u,x\rangle)q(\langle v,x\rangle)\). The chain and product rules give its derivative in direction \(u\). Unit length makes the first inner-product factor one, while the second is \(\rho\). Each derivative term is a product of polynomial ridges, so step 1 establishes all three integrability conditions of the shared Stein theorem.
steps.formula: Df(x)[u]=H_i^{\prime}(\langle u,x\rangle)q(\langle v,x\rangle)+\rho H_i(\langle u,x\rangle)q^{\prime}(\langle v,x\rangle).
steps.lean:
have hB (x : E) : HasFDerivAt B (BD x • innerSL ℝ v) x := by
    exact (q.hasDerivAt ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ).comp_hasFDerivAt x (innerSL ℝ v).hasFDerivAt
  have hf (x : E) := (hA x).mul (hB x)
  have hf' : (fun x => fderiv ℝ f x u) = fun x => AD x * B x + ρ * (A x * BD x) := by
    funext x
    change fderiv ℝ (A * B) x u = _
    rw [(hf x).fderiv]
    simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.add_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul,
      innerSL_apply_apply, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, hu, one_pow, mul_one,
      real_inner_comm u v, ρ]
    ring
  have hx : (fun x => ⟪x,u⟫_ℝ * f x) = XB := by
    funext x
    rw [real_inner_comm u x]
    simp only [XB, f, A, eval_mul, eval_X, mul_assoc]
  have hi : Integrable XB (stdGaussian E) := ridge_product_integrable (X*p) q u v
  have hAd : Integrable (fun x => AD x * B x) (stdGaussian E) :=
    ridge_product_integrable p.derivative q u v
  have hBd : Integrable (fun x => A x * BD x) (stdGaussian E) :=
    ridge_product_integrable p q.derivative u v
  have hs := GaussianIntegrationByParts.standard_gaussian_stein_of_integrable_fderiv f u
    (fun x => (hf x).differentiableAt)
    (ridge_product_integrable p q u v) (hx.symm ▸ hi)
    (hf'.symm ▸ (hAd.add (hBd.const_mul ρ)))
  rw [hx, hf', integral_add hAd (hBd.const_mul ρ), integral_const_mul] at hs

steps.title: Cancel the first derivative by the Hermite recurrence
steps.text: Apply Stein in direction \(u\). Subtract the term containing \(H_i^{\prime}\) and use \(H_{i+1}(t)=tH_i(t)-H_i^{\prime}(t)\). Only the derivative of the second polynomial remains.
steps.formula: \int H_{i+1}(\langle u,x\rangle)q(\langle v,x\rangle)\,d\gamma=\rho\int H_i(\langle u,x\rangle)q^{\prime}(\langle v,x\rangle)\,d\gamma.
steps.lean:
calc
    _ = ∫ x, XB x - AD x * B x ∂stdGaussian E := by
      apply integral_congr_ae
      filter_upwards with x
      rw [hermiteR_succ]
      simp only [p, B, AD, XB, eval_sub]
      ring
    _ = _ := by
      rw [integral_sub hi hAd]
      linarith only [hs]

steps.title: Iterate the adjoint identity
steps.text: Apply step 3 repeatedly, replacing \(q\) by its derivative at each step. The base case uses \(H_0=1\). After \(i\) iterations the entire Hermite factor has been moved onto an ordinary derivative of \(q\), with one factor of \(\rho\) at each iteration.
steps.lean:
private theorem hermite_adjoint_iterate (u v : E) (hu : ‖u‖ = 1)
    (i : ℕ) (q : Polynomial ℝ) :
    (∫ x, (hermiteR i).eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ * q.eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ ∂stdGaussian E) =
      ⟪u,v⟫_ℝ ^ i * ∫ x, (derivative^[i] q).eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ ∂stdGaussian E := by
  induction i generalizing q with
  | zero => simp [hermiteR, hermite_zero]
  | succ i ih =>
      rw [hermite_adjoint_step u v hu, ih q.derivative,
        Function.iterate_succ_apply, pow_succ]
      ring
steps.detail: Literal excerpt from the unchanged historical public-path candidate. The complete module supplies the named local facts and remains available for whole-module review.

steps.title: Evaluate the equal- and lower-degree cases
steps.text: Take \(q=H_j\). If \(i=j\), monicity and degree give \(H_i^{(i)}=i!\), whose Gaussian probability integral is \(i!\). If \(i>j\), the derivative order exceeds the polynomial degree, so the integral is zero. This includes the degree-zero case.
steps.lean:
private theorem hermite_gram_le (u v : E) (hu : ‖u‖ = 1)
    (i j : ℕ) (hji : j ≤ i) :
    (∫ x, (hermiteR i).eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ * (hermiteR j).eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ ∂stdGaussian E) =
      if i = j then (i.factorial : ℝ) * ⟪u,v⟫_ℝ ^ i else 0 := by
  rw [hermite_adjoint_iterate u v hu]
  by_cases h : i = j
  · subst j
    rw [hermiteR_top_iterate_derivative]
    simp [mul_comm]
  · have hn : (hermiteR j).natDegree < i :=
      (hermiteR_degree_le j).trans_lt (lt_of_le_of_ne hji (Ne.symm h))
    rw [iterate_derivative_eq_zero hn]
    simp [h]
steps.detail: Literal degree-comparison excerpt. The top-derivative identity is proved coefficientwise in the same module at lines 32–42, using the actual monic polynomial coefficients.

steps.title: Exchange the two projections when the first degree is smaller
steps.text: If \(i<j\), commute the two factors and apply step 5 with directions and degrees exchanged. The second unit hypothesis supplies the needed unit direction. Combine this with the integrability from step 1. There is no division by \(\rho\) or \(1-\rho^2\), so the endpoint correlations need no additional assumptions.
steps.formula: \int H_i(\langle u,x\rangle)H_j(\langle v,x\rangle)\,d\gamma=\int H_j(\langle v,x\rangle)H_i(\langle u,x\rangle)\,d\gamma.
steps.lean:
dsimp only
  simp_rw [← hermiteR_eval]
  refine ⟨ridge_product_integrable (hermiteR i) (hermiteR j) u v, ?_⟩
  rcases le_total j i with h | h
  · exact hermite_gram_le u v hu i j h
  · have hc :
        (∫ x, (hermiteR i).eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ * (hermiteR j).eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ ∂stdGaussian E) =
        ∫ x, (hermiteR j).eval ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ * (hermiteR i).eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ ∂stdGaussian E := by
      apply integral_congr_ae
      exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun _ => mul_comm _ _
    rw [hc, hermite_gram_le v u hv j i h]
    by_cases hij : i = j
    · subst j
      simp [real_inner_comm u v]
    · simp [hij, Ne.symm hij]
